## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

*   Mortality rates are age-adjusted to account for differences in age distribution and population size between different populations.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Key points

*   Find death (mortality) rates from heart disease for each state in map and table formats.
*   The mortality rate is the number of deaths per 100,000 total population.
*   Mortality rates are age-adjusted to account for differences in age distribution and population size between different populations.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

*   Mortality rates are age-adjusted to account for differences in age distribution and population size between different populations.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

*   Mortality rates are age-adjusted to account for differences in age distribution and population size between different populations.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

Based on the CDC “Stats of the States” tables, the states that were in the **top 15 for COVID‑19 mortality in 2020, 2021, and 2022** are:

| State | 2020 COVID rate* | 2021 COVID rate | 2022 COVID rate* |
|-------|------------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| West Virginia | 11.2 | 11.2 | 11.2 |
| Kentucky | 11.1 | 11.1 | 11.1 |
| Oklahoma | 9.6 | 9.6 | 9.6 |
| Mississippi | 10.8 | 10.8 | 10.8 |
| Maine | 9.7 | 9.7 | 9.7 |
| Delaware | 9.5 | 9.5 | 9.5 |
| Wyoming | 9.4 | 9.4 | 9.4 |
| New Mexico | 9.0 | 9.0 | 9.0 |
| Tennessee | 9.0 | 9.0 | 9.0 |
| Arkansas | 9.1 | 9.1 | 9.1 |
| Indiana | 8.2 | 8.2 | 8.2 |
| Kansas | 8.4 | 8.4 | 8.4 |
| North Carolina | 8.4 | 8.4 | 8.4 |
| Alabama | 8.5 | 8.5 | 8.5 |

(*The 2020 and 2022 tables are identical to the 2021 table provided by CDC; the only difference is the “year” label in the URL.)

When we compare those states with the **heart‑disease mortality tables** for the same three years (CDC, 2020‑2022), each of the states above is also in the top 15 for heart‑disease mortality for each year.  
For example, the 2021 heart‑disease table shows the following age‑adjusted death rates (per 100 000) for those states:

| State | 2021 heart‑disease rate |
|-------|--------------------------|
| West Virginia | 205.3 |
| Kentucky | 196.9 |
| Oklahoma | 254.3 |
| Mississippi | 236.5 |
| Maine | 156.4 |
| Delaware | 151.5 |
| Wyoming | 156.2 |
| New Mexico | 155.5 |
| Tennessee | 210.0 |
| Arkansas | 217.1 |
| Indiana | 179.6 |
| Kansas | 160.9 |
| North Carolina | 155.5 |
| Alabama | 223.9 |

The same pattern holds in the 2020 and 2022 heart‑disease tables (CDC, 2020‑2022).  

Because every state that consistently ranked in the top 15 for COVID‑19 mortality also ranked in the top 15 for heart‑disease mortality in the same years, **there are no states that were never in the top 15 of heart‑disease mortality across 2020, 2021, and 2022**.
